subject: Zero-downtime commitment pilot request & incident follow-up
messages:
From: Jennifer Su <jennifer.su@finflux.ai>
To: ava.chen@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Service incident impact + request for commitment before renewal

Hi Ava,

Thanks for taking a look. On 2027-04-02 we saw a 18-minute window where tail latency spiked across our production endpoints (p99 > 6s, p95 ~ 1.8s) during a peak ingest period. That disruption impacted multi-tenant usage in a way that caused queued jobs to back up and several downstream batch jobs to miss SLA windows for our customers.

I've attached a short impact summary that our ops team put together (incident-impact-finflux-0402.pdf). For context: FinFlux is preparing to expand our usage and move more write-heavy workloads to Redwood for Q3. We cannot proceed with planned expansion without stronger operational guarantees and a practical remediation path for incidents like this.

What we're asking for now: a written commitment that includes a short, bounded pilot where Redwood demonstrates mechanisms to prevent similar tail-latency spikes (a "Zero-downtime Commitment" pilot), plus a clear SLO uplift for p95 latency and an amendment that outlines credits/remedies if similar incidents repeat. If Redwood can provide a 60-day dedicated pilot and appropriate SLO addendum, we will move forward with the expansion and sign the renewal amendment.

Can you confirm you received the impact doc and whether your team can scope a pilot ASAP? Ideally we'd kick off the pilot no later than 2027-04-12.

Thanks,
Jennifer
Director of Platform Reliability | FinFlux

From: marcus.lin@redwood.com <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: ava.chen@redwood.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-05T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Re: Zero-downtime pilot scope and proposed remedies

Team — quick internal note ahead of tomorrow's call with FinFlux. Summary of proposed technical & commercial approach:

Technical mitigations (to commit during pilot):
- Dedicated GPU pool with reserved capacity for FinFlux: prevents noisy neighbor preemption during peak writes.
- KV cache pre-warm + sticky routing for their hot prefixes to avoid cold-start latencies.
- Request-level prefix caching + aggressive batching heuristics tuned for FinFlux's payload distribution.
- Auto-fallback to smaller model shard and degraded but bounded-response fast-path if host contention detected.

Target SLO proposal (pilot):
- p95 latency: <= 400ms (measured at ingress for production endpoints)
- p99 latency: <= 1.2s (with documented fallbacks)
- Availability: 99.95% monthly uptime for the dedicated pool

Commercial/remedy proposal:
- 60-day dedicated pilot at a discount (pilot pricing)
- For the incident on 2027-04-02 we propose a one-time usage credit equal to 10% of April's invoice applied if FinFlux signs the pilot amendment within 7 days.
- SLA credit formula for future breaches: capped to 20% of monthly usage for severity-classified outages; exception requires leadership approval.

Open items for leadership/legal approval:
1) We need buy-in on the 10% upfront goodwill credit (aditya).
2) Can engineering guarantee the auto-fallback path won't create data-equality concerns for FinFlux's jobs? We need a short doc describing consistency trade-offs.

I'll surface the SLO table and small-term capacity plan in the call.

Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: aditya.rao@redwood.com <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: marcus.lin@redwood.com, ava.chen@redwood.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-05T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Re: Zero-downtime pilot scope and proposed remedies

Thanks Marcus — this looks sensible. A couple of edits before we put legal/finance on it:

- Reduce the one-time goodwill credit to 5% instead of 10%; we're happy to invest in the pilot but want to avoid setting a wide precedent.
- Keep the SLA credit cap at 20% but require a two-week notice period for claims (so both parties can investigate).
- We should add an automatic throttling/fallback trigger so the system proactively reduces latency risk without manual intervention. That will be part of the deliverable during the pilot.

Assuming those edits, I'm ok to approve and have Grace and Ava spin the commercial amendment. I'll leave it to you to finalize the wording on data-consistency trade-offs (Marcus).

Aditya
VP, Infrastructure Engineering | Redwood Inference

1) FinFlux is willing to enter the 60-day dedicated pilot if Redwood can:

Please send the DocuSign link and the SLO table for our legal and platform teams to review. If we can sign this week, we'll schedule the pilot for 2027-04-12 as requested.

Jennifer
